The daily selection period starts at 20:: The daily selection period starts at 20:00 Europe/Berlin. At most one successful selection is made per unchanged source/settings contract and period. Initial activation uses a valid available forecast; a restart preserves a qualified selection for the same period. Defaults: below 0 °C = 30%, from 0 °C through 5 °C = 20%, above 5 °C = 10%. This replaces only the effective EMS minimum SoC; maximum SoC and morning/afternoon/late targets remain unchanged. Use a forecast for the upcoming night: day1 is tomorrow, while day0 is today. The source must be a confirmed, valid numeric value in °C within the configured maximum age. An invalid or missing forecast retains the last valid selection; before the first valid selection, the fixed minimum applies and the fallback is shown. A later valid forecast can complete the current period with its actual selection time. Thresholds must be ordered and all selected reserves must be below the configured maximum SoC. No external SI endpoint is written and no grid-charging or output release is enabled.

Select exactly the heads configured in t: Select exactly the heads configured in the standard driver: head 1, heads 1–2 or heads 1–3. Unselected configured heads are not permitted. This setting does not enable battery control.
The unchanged SunEnergy standard adapter: The unchanged SunEnergy standard adapter remains the device driver. Set its control mode to Off, with each selected head in local mode LM=1 and manual grid mode MM=0. The EMS writes each heads.N.control.GS directly, never a virtual house-grid signal. GS and GP are positive for discharge and negative for charge; EMS internal power is positive for charge. Fresh per-head rawResponse and online feedback are required. Missing or invalid head data blocks the output and retains the unconfirmed power reserve. Acknowledged GS alone is not physical power feedback.
SoC balancing prefers lower-SoC heads wh: SoC balancing prefers lower-SoC heads when charging and higher-SoC heads when discharging. The reported ON pack count weights each head's relative capacity; it is not an online flag. Per-head limits, measured device limits and the shared total budget remain binding. All requested head powers have the same direction: the EMS does not charge one head while discharging another. Exact equality is not guaranteed while power, SoC or availability limits differ.
In this mode the EMS reads SoC (SC), onl: In this mode the EMS reads SoC (SC), online pack count (ON), actual AC power (GP), device SoC limits and device/model power limits from coherent per-head responses. Separate SoC and DC-power mappings are not used. User targets, permissions and additional power limits remain unchanged. No dynamic BMS charge limit, efficiency or battery temperature is inferred.
Automatic capacity is the sum of online: Automatic capacity is the sum of online packs (ON) multiplied by the explicitly entered capacity of one equal-sized pack. ON is an online pack count, not the nominal installed capacity. Confirm the pack size from your device documentation; no default pack size is assumed. Missing or invalid data for any selected head, or a missing pack size, makes automatic capacity unknown and prevents a valid battery forecast. The manual capacity is not used as a silent fallback.
